note: Licences read from each repository's licence file (raw.githubusercontent.com) and HEAD commits from git on the 'checked' date. Licences and maintenance change: re-check before relying on them. Not legal advice.

tools.name: OpenBB (Open Data Platform)
tools.description: Open-source Python toolset (installed as `pip install openbb`) that connects public, licensed and proprietary financial data sources and exposes them to Python, Excel, REST and AI-agent (MCP) consumers.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Copyright (c) 2021-2026 OpenBB Inc. / All files in this repository are licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0."
tools.caveats: Formerly Gamestonk Terminal: README no longer mentions it, but git ls-remote of github.com/GamestonkTerminal/GamestonkTerminal redirects to this repo (same HEAD SHA). The terminal-style UI (OpenBB Workspace, pro.openbb.co) is a separate enterprise product, not this repo. Many data providers need your own API keys or paid plans. Default branch is 'develop'.

tools.name: Fincept Terminal
tools.description: Desktop financial-analytics terminal that combines market data, analytics and AI automation, from a company that also sells paid Enterprise and data plans.
tools.license: Custom: AGPL-3.0 text plus a 'Dual Licensing Notice' and 'Additional Restrictions' (commercial/internal use requires paid Fincept Commercial License)
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 19 November 2007 / Copyright (C) 2025-2026 Fincept Corporation" followed by "DUAL LICENSING NOTICE ... The AGPL-3.0 option is NOT available for Commercial Use" and "Internal use within any for-profit organization, government body, fund, or revenue-generating non-profit is Commercial Use and requires a paid Commercial License."
tools.caveats: The licence file adds a dual-licensing notice to the AGPL-3.0 text: it states that the AGPL option is not available for commercial use, including internal use at for-profit organizations, funds and government bodies, which require a paid commercial licence. Read the full licence before any commercial use.

tools.name: Ghostfolio
tools.description: Self-hostable web application for tracking holdings in stocks, ETFs and cryptocurrencies across multiple platforms and analysing portfolio composition and performance.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 19 November 2007"
tools.caveats: AGPL network clause: if you host a modified version for others, you must offer them its source. A paid hosted 'Ghostfolio Premium' exists. -only vs -or-later not determined (only LICENSE file read).

tools.name: bqplot
tools.description: 2-D interactive plotting library for Jupyter, based on the Grammar of Graphics, in which every plot component is an ipywidget.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"; later sections note d3 colour schemes (BSD-3-Clause) and ColorBrewer files bundled
tools.caveats: Finance-relevant: a general Jupyter plotting widget that is useful for market dashboards. Bundles some third-party BSD-licensed colour-scheme code.

tools.name: ipydatagrid
tools.description: Fast, customisable data-grid widget for displaying and styling tabular data (e.g. pandas DataFrames) in Jupyter Notebook and JupyterLab.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.txt: "Copyright (c) 2019 / All rights reserved. / Redistribution and use in source and binary forms..." with 3 clauses incl. "Neither the name of the copyright holder..."
tools.caveats: Finance-relevant as a Jupyter table/grid widget. The copyright line in LICENSE.txt names no holder ('Copyright (c) 2019').

tools.name: Memray
tools.description: Memory profiler for Python that traces allocations in Python code, native extensions and the interpreter, and produces reports such as flame graphs.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
tools.caveats: Not finance-specific; a general Python tooling project from Bloomberg.

tools.name: Comdb2
tools.description: Clustered relational database that uses optimistic concurrency control and supports snapshot and serializable isolation. Bloomberg has developed it since 2004.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Copyright 2015, 2017, Bloomberg Finance L.P. / Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the \"License\")"
tools.caveats: Not finance-specific; general infrastructure (RDBMS).

tools.name: PyStack
tools.description: Tool that prints the stack traces of a running Python process or a Python core dump, including native frames.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
tools.caveats: Not finance-specific. README badge says Linux only.

tools.name: QuantLib
tools.description: C++ library for quantitative finance that provides a framework for modelling, pricing, trading and risk management of financial instruments.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.TXT (not LICENSE): opens "Copyright (C) 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003 RiskMap srl ..." and contains the 3 BSD clauses incl. "Neither the names of the copyright holders nor the names of the QuantLib Group..."
tools.caveats: The license file is LICENSE.TXT, so the standard LICENSE/LICENSE.txt probes 404. README: 'Non-Copylefted Free Software and OSI Certified Open Source Software'. Python bindings live in a separate repo (QuantLib-SWIG).

tools.name: Zipline Reloaded
tools.description: Community-maintained continuation of Quantopian's Zipline, an event-driven Python backtesting engine that works with pandas and the PyData stack.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
tools.caveats: Maintained mainly by one person (README). Last commit was about 11 months before this check. Needs separate data bundles.

tools.name: backtrader
tools.description: Python platform for backtesting and live trading, with data feeds, indicators, analysers, plotting and broker integrations such as Interactive Brokers and Oanda.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007"; source header backtrader/__init__.py: "either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version"
tools.caveats: Copyleft (GPL): distributing derived software requires releasing its source under GPL. Effectively dormant: last commit 2023-04-19. The built-in Yahoo feed in the README example may no longer work.

tools.name: Backtesting.py
tools.description: Lightweight Python library for backtesting trading strategies on pandas OHLC data, with built-in optimisation and interactive Bokeh result plots.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.md: "### GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 19 November 2007"; setup.py: license='AGPL-3.0', classifier "GNU Affero General Public License v3 or later (AGPLv3+)"
tools.caveats: AGPL: the network clause applies if you offer a modified version as a hosted service.

tools.name: vectorbt
tools.description: Python library for fast, vectorised backtesting and strategy research on pandas/NumPy/Numba (with an optional Rust engine), able to test many parameter combinations at once. It is the community edition of the commercial VectorBT PRO.
tools.license: Custom: Apache-2.0 with Commons Clause v1.0
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.md: "“Commons Clause” License Condition v1.0 ... the License does not grant to you, the right to Sell the Software." then "Software: vectorbt / License: Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause / Licensor: Oleg Polakow" followed by Apache 2.0 text
tools.caveats: Commons Clause bans selling the software or a product or service whose value comes substantially from it, so this is source-available, not OSI open source. The paid VectorBT PRO has more features.

tools.name: QuantStats
tools.description: Python library for portfolio performance analytics: risk/return metrics (Sharpe, drawdowns, etc.), plots and HTML tear-sheet reports, now with Monte Carlo simulation.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.txt: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004"

tools.name: LEAN
tools.description: QuantConnect's event-driven algorithmic trading engine (C#, with Python strategy support) for backtesting and live trading across multiple asset classes.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
tools.caveats: Engine is open source. QuantConnect's cloud platform and many datasets are commercial. Can also be categorised as backtesting.

tools.name: yfinance
tools.description: Python library that downloads market data (prices, fundamentals, etc.) from Yahoo! Finance into pandas.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.txt: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004"
tools.caveats: Unofficial wrapper around Yahoo Finance endpoints, not affiliated with Yahoo. README quote: "yfinance is **not** affiliated, endorsed, or vetted by Yahoo, Inc. It's an open-source tool that uses Yahoo's publicly available APIs, and is intended for research and educational purposes." and "Remember - the Yahoo! finance API is intended for personal use only." It tells users to read Yahoo's terms of use. (README says 'publicly available APIs' and never uses the word 'scrape'.) The code license does not cover the data. Endpoints can break or rate-limit without notice.

tools.name: pandas-datareader
tools.description: Python library that loads remote macroeconomic, policy and factor data (e.g. FRED, Fama/French, World Bank, OECD, Eurostat) into pandas.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE.md: "pandas is distributed under a 3-clause (\"Simplified\" or \"New\") BSD license" then "Copyright (c) 2011-2012, Lambda Foundry, Inc. and PyData Development Team" with 3 BSD clauses
tools.caveats: LICENSE.md is the pandas license text reused (its banner says 'BSD Simplified License', but the clauses are 3-clause). README now focuses on macro and factor sources, not stock-price feeds. Each data source has its own terms.

tools.name: Apache ECharts
tools.description: JavaScript charting and visualisation library (rendered via ZRender) for interactive, highly customisable charts, including candlestick and other financial charts.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"; appended 'Apache ECharts Subcomponents' section lists d3.js-derived files under BSD-3-Clause
tools.caveats: Some subcomponents are BSD-3-Clause (d3).

tools.name: plotly.js
tools.description: Standalone JavaScript data-visualisation library that also powers Plotly for Python and R, with dozens of chart types including financial (OHLC/candlestick) and 3D charts.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2016-2024 Plotly Technologies Inc."

tools.name: TA-Lib (Python wrapper)
tools.description: Cython-based Python wrapper for the TA-Lib C library, which provides 150+ technical-analysis indicators and candlestick-pattern recognition.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "# BSD 2-Clause License / Redistribution and use in source and binary forms..." (2 clauses, no non-endorsement clause)
tools.caveats: Needs the underlying TA-Lib C library installed separately (README). The C library has its own license (not checked here).

tools.name: Qlib
tools.description: Microsoft's AI-oriented quantitative investment platform covering the research-to-production workflow, with support for supervised learning, market-dynamics modelling and reinforcement learning.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "MIT License / Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation."
tools.caveats: README promotes the companion RD-Agent project (LLM agents for factor mining). Bundled data is for research, and data-source terms apply.

tools.name: FinRL
tools.description: Open-source framework for financial reinforcement learning, kept as the original educational, benchmarking and research-prototyping library.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "The MIT License (MIT) / Copyright (c) 2024 AI4Finance Foundation Inc."
tools.caveats: README points users to the successor FinRL-X / FinRL-Trading for production and live trading. 'FinRL®' is a registered mark.

tools.name: NautilusTrader
tools.description: Rust-native, event-driven trading engine with a Python control layer that covers research, deterministic backtest simulation and live execution across multiple venues and asset classes.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007"
tools.caveats: Weak copyleft (LGPL). Default branch is 'develop'. -only vs -or-later not determined.

tools.name: Hummingbot
tools.description: Open-source framework for building and running automated trading bots (e.g. market making, arbitrage) on centralised and decentralised crypto exchanges.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
tools.caveats: Crypto-focused. Live trading risks real funds, and exchange ToS and API terms apply.

tools.name: Lightweight Charts
tools.description: Small, fast HTML5 canvas library from TradingView for interactive financial charts (candlestick, line, area, etc.), extensible with plugins.
tools.license_evidence: LICENSE: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"; NOTICE: "TradingView Lightweight Charts™ / Copyright (с) 2025 TradingView, Inc."
tools.caveats: Attribution required: README says "This license requires specifying TradingView as the product creator. You shall add the \"attribution notice\" from the NOTICE file and a link to https://www.tradingview.com/ to the page of your website or mobile application" (the attributionLogo option meets the link requirement). This is not the full TradingView charting library, which is licensed separately.

tools.name: Bloomberg BLPAPI (Bloomberg API SDK)
tools.description: Bloomberg's official SDK (C++, Python, etc.) for programmatic access to Bloomberg market data and services through Desktop API, Server API or B-PIPE connections.
tools.license: Custom: LicenseRef-Bloomberg-BLPAPI (proprietary Bloomberg license; official text NOT verified)
tools.license_evidence: Official page and PyPI could not be read: www.bloomberg.com and blpapi.bloomberg.com are blocked by this environment's egress proxy, WebFetch permission timed out, and https://pypi.org/pypi/blpapi/json returns HTTP 404 (no 'blpapi' project on PyPI; the Python package is distributed from https://blpapi.bloomberg.com/repository/releases/python/). Secondary evidence: conda-forge/blpapi-feedstock recipe/recipe.yaml (HEAD 513a7de2fee34803a0fe64a0b56443d5256e6e6d, 2026-09-09), v3.26.8.1: "license: LicenseRef-Bloomberg-BLPAPI", "license_file: License.txt", "summary: Python SDK for Bloomberg BLPAPI", source url https://blpapi.bloomberg.com/repository/releases/python/blpapi-3.26.8.1.tar.gz. Bloomberg's own GitHub repo bloomberg/blpapi-node (HEAD 762e61d7593f6f4c24801b3ee685f27760d6b2a8, last commit 2015-06-01, MIT-licensed wrapper) README: "This module requires: ... Bloomberg Desktop API (DAPI), Server API (SAPI), or [B-PIPE] subscription". bloomberg/blpapi-http README: "Note that a functioning BLPAPI endpoint is required to use this HTTP wrapper."
tools.caveats: Data access needs a Bloomberg entitlement (Desktop API, Server API or B-PIPE), per Bloomberg's own blpapi-node README; the SDK licence is a custom Bloomberg licence (conda-forge records LicenseRef-Bloomberg-BLPAPI), not an OSI open-source licence. Bloomberg's official terms page could not be read from our build environment; check it directly. Data redistribution is governed by your Bloomberg agreement.
